mathematical_review: Every operation generated by encode has positive length. For total literal bytes B, COPY count C, and LITERAL count L, pack must serialize at least B + 13*C + 5*L bytes plus at least max(ceil(B/61440), ceil((C+L)/256)) frame headers/exchanges of 137 bytes each.
Literal splitting can only increase operation prefixes and frame count. The bound is used only to reject candidates, never to admit an unmaterialized recipe.

Rejecting when lower_bound + 32 >= Raw cost preserves the original strict Sparse < Raw requirement. Rejecting aligned when its lower bound is at least the existing actual cost preserves the original simple-first equality rule.
If the simple candidate remains ineligible after packing, min(actual_simple_cost, Raw_cost-32) is still a safe aligned rejection ceiling. The final legacy eligibility filter remains present.

Nonempty input Raw cost is at least 134, so saturating subtraction of 32 does not change the accepted-input arithmetic. Empty target returns before the bound. Generated input lengths and operation counts keep the new checked sums within usize on the qualified target, so no new accepted-input error path is introduced.
Named 13-byte and 5-byte constants substitute identical values in pack; serialization and decoder code otherwise remain unchanged.

With current constants, a valid generated frame body is at most 9 + 13*256 + 61440 = 64777 bytes, below 65480. A body-size-first fixture cannot be generated; the explicit proof regression is appropriate.
correctness_and_security_review: Finite tests compare actual ordered frame vectors and operation counts to the immutable encoder, reconstruct with both decoders, and cover empty/binary data, append/truncate, insertion/deletion, Raw equality, simple/aligned ties, frame/op splits, invalid recipes, and size limits.

The production diff changes only sender-side sparse candidate materialization. Authentication, authorization, missing-base behavior, receiver validation, cache publication, and protocol encodings are unchanged.
The sender ceiling remains 16 MiB; larger core API checks do not qualify larger network transfers. No prefix-codec candidate is skipped by this milestone.

The test-only forwarding allocator and diagnostic allocator keep unsafe code outside the production library. The diagnostic forwards valid layouts to System, preserves the old allocation on failed growth, and copies only min(old_size,new_size) bytes between distinct live allocations.

Diagnostic tracking is bounded and thread-local; process-wide flags require its documented single-threaded use and serial diagnostic tests. Registry/callback failures fail qualification. New discoveries stop at encode return; retained buffers stay tracked through drop.

The normal timed executable excludes custom allocation tracking at compile time. The diagnostic's forced-moving alloc-copy-free peak is actual requested frame-buffer capacity under that policy, not production allocator overlap or RSS.

The local harness launches its current executable through argv, refuses existing evidence paths with create_new, synchronizes rows, and preserves child failures. Its source revision is explicitly caller supplied and still requires external source/executable custody.
